title: Rotate Image
description: Given an n x n matrix representing an image, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in place, without allocating another matrix.

reference.use_case: Rotating a square image or grid by 90 degrees in place without allocating a second copy.
system_examples: Image editors and phone galleries — rotating photos
Games — rotating tile maps and pieces (e.g. Tetris piece rotation)
Embedded and GPU code — in-place matrix transforms under tight memory limits
reference.explanation: A 90° clockwise rotation equals a transpose followed by reversing each row (or a four-way cyclic swap per layer), in O(n²) time and O(1) extra space. In-place transforms matter when memory is tight, such as on embedded devices or with very large images.
